title: Sponge gourd Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Sponge gourd Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Sponge gourd nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and potassium in patola, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Sponge gourd nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your patola (sponge gourd) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, magnesium, phosphorus and boron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Ridge gourd (the angled patola) leaf gone pale yellow green from nitrogen shortage
heroImage.credit: Orka, Uddin, Toushique and Hossain, OLID I dataset, CC BY 4.0, via Zenodo

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, magnesium and phosphorus move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which sponge gourd nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a sponge gourd nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest sponge gourd nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in sponge gourd

blocks.alt: Ridge gourd (the angled patola) leaf gone pale yellow green from nitrogen shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Orka, Uddin, Toushique and Hossain, OLID I dataset, CC BY 4.0, via Zenodo

blocks.text: Older leaves on the vine turn pale and then yellow, and the yellowing climbs as the shortage grows. Vines grow slowly and set fewer, smaller and paler fruits. You see it most at this stage: rapid vine growth and fruit set, when cucurbits most often run short.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in patola
Sandy soils, heavy rain, low organic matter, and no side dressing before fruiting.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage leaves the veins green on old leaves. Downy mildew gives angular yellow patches between veins. To be sure, old leaves yellow first. Soil test and leaf tissue test.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Before fruits form, side dress urea or ammonium sulfate in one or two doses at the soil test rate. For bottle gourd, a related gourd, give a urea leaf spray at 10 grams per liter of water (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) every 15 days. Side dress 5 to 10 grams of Urea 46 0 0 a plant, about 1 to 2 bags per hectare, every two to three weeks from flowering, and water it in.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea (46 0 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Crown Champion Ammonium Sulfate** by Aqua Hydroponic Prime Ventures (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur), **Agripower 46 0 0 (Locally Blended) Coated** by Green Acres Agri Tech and **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, add manure to the hills before planting and side dress before fruit set.
Potassium deficiency in sponge gourd
Older leaves yellow and scorch along the edges, then brown and cup. Roots are weak and stems slender. Fruit filling suffers. You see it most at this stage: fruiting.
Why potassium deficiency happens in patola
Sandy or acid soils, heavy rain, and urea only feeding.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage yellows between the veins first. To be sure, soil test for potassium and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For bottle gourd, a related gourd, give a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) with a sticker. A usual dose is 1 to 2 bags of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Sulfate of potash 0 0 50 per hectare, split from flowering to fruit fill.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash (MOP)** by Atlas Fertilizer (0 0 60), **Simplot Sulfate 0 0 50** by Nutranta, **Potassium Nitrate** by Parafield (13 0 46) and **Qrop Mix Production 14 0 23 plus 13 Cao** by Farmtech Agriland (14 0 23 with 9.3 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash at planting and at flowering. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.
Magnesium deficiency in sponge gourd

Yellowing between the veins starts on the oldest leaves and moves up the vine. The yellow tissue may brown, die and drop out, leaving holes. You see it most at this stage: fast growth while fruits enlarge.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in patola
Sandy soils with low holding capacity, low pH, dry years, and heavy potash, lime or ammonium fertilizer.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage yellows the whole leaf. Manganese toxicity on very acid soil gives bronze spots. To be sure, soil test for magnesium, potassium and pH.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

Hold soil pH near 6.5, and feed Epsom salt through drip lines when needed. Leaf sprays rarely fix a serious shortage. For bottle gourd, give magnesium sulfate in a band at about 80 kg per hectare. For quick help, spray Magnesium sulfate at 1 to 2 percent (160 to 320 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) two or three times, 10 to 14 days apart.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium), **DDDD Planter's Choice Magnesium Sulphate Monohydrate** by Modern Time (15.1 percent magnesium) and **Zetryl MAG 9** by Zetryl Chem (9 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomite on acid soil before planting. Test the soil every two or three years. Keep potash in balance with magnesium and calcium.
Phosphorus deficiency in sponge gourd

Growth is held back without yellowing. Stems are slender, leaves are small and darker green, undersides may turn reddish purple, and flowering and fruiting are delayed. You see it most at this stage: seedling and early vine growth.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in patola
Acid or iron rich soils, low organic matter, cold or waterlogged soil, and no phosphorus at planting.
How to tell it apart
Root knot nematodes also stunt vines. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply phosphorus in the hill based on the soil test, and lime very acid soil. Follow the soil test for the rate. A usual basal dose is 4 to 6 bags of Complete 14 14 14 per hectare, 10 to 20 grams a hill, mixed into the soil at transplanting.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Philphos 18 46 0 (Di Ammonium Phosphate)**, **Atlas Super Gro (16 20 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Granular Single Super Phosphate** by La Filipina (0 18 0 with 11 percent sulfur) and **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals (0 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use complete fertilizer or 16 20 0 in the hill at planting.
Boron deficiency in sponge gourd

New leaves and stalks are light, brittle and deformed, internodes are short and the tips rosette. Young fruits drop, and fruits may show corky marks or cracks. You see it most at this stage: flowering and fruit set.
Why boron deficiency happens in patola
Sandy soils, overlimed soils, low organic matter and drought.
How to tell it apart
Fruit fly damage also drops young fruits but leaves stay normal and maggots are inside. To be sure, soil test for boron and a leaf tissue test. In a soil test, less than 0.5 ppm of boron is low.
What to apply for boron deficiency

For bottle gourd, a related gourd, give borax at about 10 kg per hectare in the soil, or a borax spray at 1 gram per liter of water (16 grams in a 16 liter sprayer). Do not repeat doses without a test. Give boron before flowering: flowers and fruit set need it most.

Sold here with boron: **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl Chem (11 percent boron), **Fertibagra 15G** by Unilox Far East Resources (14.6 percent boron), **B17 (Boric Acid)** by Newman Chemicals (17 percent boron) and **Better Yield** by Bacphil Planters Fertilizer (0 0 0.9 with 10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add a small boron dose to the basal fertilizer on sandy fields. Test the soil every two or three years. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any sponge gourd nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your patola needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Sponge gourd nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my patola leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: older leaves turn yellow, vines grow slowly and fruits stay small and pale. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at magnesium deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in sponge gourd?
items.a: Before fruits form, side dress urea or ammonium sulfate in one or two doses at the soil test rate. For bottle gourd, a related gourd, give a urea leaf spray at 10 grams per liter of water (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) every 15 days.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in sponge gourd?
items.a: Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For bottle gourd, a related gourd, give a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) with a sticker.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes magnesium deficiency in sponge gourd?
items.a: Hold soil pH near 6.5, and feed Epsom salt through drip lines when needed. Leaf sprays rarely fix a serious shortage.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my patola lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the sponge gourd nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
